correctness.rationale: All 3d line components and three exceptional curves and all nodes are determined from the Hessian and three-pencil intersection equation; the reduced Laplacian has the exact five-generator integral presentation stated in RESULT.md. The primitive t_a change of basis, unit-coefficient eliminations, p-adic Smith reductions including 3|(2d+1), and determinant establish the formula for every d>=3. A separate edge-constructed graph Smith computation was replayed for all d=3..12; these finite tests are only corroboration. Boundary genus, stability, hypotheses, and Néron interpretation were checked.

value.rationale: The boundary is the minimal normal-crossing resolution of the entire geometrically intrinsic maximal-tangent line divisor of smooth Fermat curves, not an arbitrary graph selection. The theorem gives a uniform complete integral classification for all degrees, including a sharp mod-three change in the number of cyclic factors that cannot be deduced from the classical incidence counts or tree number. It determines geometric Néron component groups of any semistable degeneration with exactly this fiber, a natural invariant of stable-curve degenerations. Its dimension-free integral reduction makes the family computable without enumerating enormous Laplacians.
